To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the oxygen and hydrogen stable isotope compositions of tissues in rodents are a function of diet, water source, and ontogenetic stage.

(a) the isotopic composition recorded in tissues reflects a mixture of the isotopic composition in the food and the isotopic composition from the water, (b) the isotopic signature of water is more important in the isotopic record of tissues in animals from the same geographic area but with different diets, and (c) the isotopic signatures of the tissues reflect the age of the animal

(1) the oxygen and hydrogen isotopic composition of drinking water is recorded in the tissues of rats raised on diets with constant isotopic values, (2) the magnitude of the recorded signal varies by tissue and age, and (3) the isotopic composition in tissues of rats raised in two different hydrological settings is statistically distinct
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isotopic composition in tissues of rodents, which is influenced by the isotopic composition and the amount of water and food ingested.
the impact of diet, water, and ontogeny on the δ 18 O, and δD values in the tissues of rodents.
the effects of diet, water source and ontogenetic age on the δD and δ18O values of tissues in rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the magnitude of the isotopic signal recorded in tissues is highly sensitive to the age and size of the animal, the isotopic composition and variability of the diet, and the isotopic composition, variability and source of the drinking water.
the δD of subcutaneous fat and δ 18 OP of enamel apatite are the most promising tissue types for the reconstruction of the isotopic history of the water source of a rodent.
the isotopic composition in tissues of rodents, or other mammals, can be used to determine the isotopic composition and source of drinking water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tissue δD and, in particular, tissue δ 18O values are sensitive to the δD and δ18O of drinking water and food, and that these isotopic values are sensitive to organism ontogeny.
the magnitude of the isotopic signal recorded in the tissues of heterotrophs is a function of the isotopic difference between the drinking water and food source.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the isotopic composition in different tissues of the same organism are not always identical.

the magnitude of the isotopic difference between the local water and food resources is the most important factor in determining the isotopic composition in tissues of interest to the palaeontological and ecological communities.

the isotopic compositions of tissues from rodents can be used to reconstruct past environmental conditions, and that the choice of tissue and animal ontogeny will influence the precision with which environmental information can be recovered.
